reviewer: Claude (independent reviewer agent, Anthropic; standing in while OpenAI Codex is offline; not Codex)

findings.evidence: The W-2 field asks for 'Medicare wages, W-2 box 5' and the adapter (src/adapters/self-employment-tax.js:147) passes it as socialSecurityWages, which reduces the wage base exactly like Schedule SE line 8a. Line 8a is W-2 boxes 3 + 7 (plus tier 1 railroad retirement compensation), with lines 8b/8c adding Form 4137 tips and Form 8919 wages (IRS Schedule SE, corroborated by search only). Box 5 can be much larger than box 3, e.g. Medicare-only state or local government employees (box 3 = 0). Reproduced: $100,000 of Medicare-only wages and $100,000 profit for 2026 give SS tax $10,478.00 from the calculator vs $11,451.40 correct (12.4% x 92,350), an understatement of $973.40. The page copy (src/pages/self-employment-tax-calculator.js:159-160) says results 'can differ slightly', which is not true in that case.
findings.recommendation: Ask for Social Security wages (box 3 + box 7, plus tier 1 RRTA compensation) and Medicare wages (box 5) separately, defaulting Medicare wages to the SS figure, or at least change the hint to box 3 + box 7 and reword the assumption to name the Medicare-only employee case and its size.

findings.evidence: Only Form 8959 Part II (Additional Medicare Tax on SE income) is computed. Part I tax on wages above the threshold is ignored, yet when the Part II amount is 0 the card reads 'None: under the $200,000.00 threshold'. Reproduced: W-2 wages $300,000 with profit $0, and W-2 wages $250,000 with profit $433, both show 'None: under the $200,000.00 threshold' although 0.9% applies to the wages above $200,000 (Part I). The lede (src/pages/self-employment-tax-calculator.js:74) promises to show 'whether the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax applies'.
findings.recommendation: Label the figure 'Additional Medicare Tax on self-employment income' and replace the 'None: under the threshold' note with a condition-aware message, e.g. when Medicare wages exceed the threshold, say that Additional Medicare Tax on wages (Form 8959 Part I) applies and is not shown. Narrow the lede to match.

findings.evidence: Exact half-cent values are rounded down by binary floating point at display: the W-2 example Additional Medicare 0.009 x 38,525 = 346.725 shows $346.72 (hand rounding $346.73); the table row for $150,000 shows SE tax $21,194.32 for an exact 21,194.325 ($21,194.33). Meanwhile Medicare 4,017.225 shows $4,017.23 and 277.875 shows $277.88, so a reader hand-checking sees inconsistent rounding. Independent Decimal recomputation in review-work/recompute.py.
findings.recommendation: Round to cents with a decimal-safe half-up (e.g. Math.round((x + Number.EPSILON*x) * 100)/100 or scaled integer arithmetic) in formatCurrency or before display; or pick worked examples without half-cent results.

findings.evidence: Profit $433.13 gives net earnings 399.996, displayed as 'Net earnings of $400.00 are under $400, so no self-employment tax is due.' The math is right (399.996 < 400) but the sentence contradicts itself on screen.
findings.recommendation: Show net earnings with floor-to-cent in this message (e.g. $399.99), or phrase it 'are less than $400 ($399.996)'.

findings.evidence: The page comment claims the sources were 'Read directly by the Codex audit on 2026-10-18', while src/content/site.js:287 says the page is not built 'until its IRS and SSA sources are verified directly (Codex audit ZA-002)'. No SSA source is cited; the 2026 $184,500 figure is attributed to IRS Topic 751. This reviewer could not open the IRS/SSA pages; web-search snippets corroborate $176,100 (2025), $184,500 (2026) and Topic 751 stating the 2026 cap, but that is not a direct read.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two comments; record who read which page and when; consider citing SSA's contribution and benefit base page for the wage bases before going live.

findings.evidence: The 'independent line-by-line reference' mirrors the engine's own structure and constants (same 400 test on 0.9235 x profit, same min/max) and medicareWages is always >= socialSecurityWages in the random cases, so it cannot catch a shared semantic error such as A2-001. The page's methodology claim (src/pages/self-employment-tax-calculator.js:172-174) is literally true but overstates assurance.
findings.recommendation: Add fixed cases taken from published IRS worked examples or a Schedule SE filled by hand, including medicareWages > socialSecurityWages with SS wages 0.

findings.evidence: Negative values use two different minus signs: cash flow and cost lines use U+2212 via signed(), but percentages use toFixed ('-0.70%', '-25.63%', '-1.70%') and the cap-rate note uses formatCurrency ('-$5,100.00 NOI'). Same on the page (src/pages/rental-property-calculator.js:21, cash-on-cash '-0.70%'). DSCR prints '-0.28'.
findings.recommendation: Route percentages, ratios and the NOI note through one signed formatter so every negative uses the same sign.

findings.evidence: With 0% down and no closing or repair costs, cash invested is $0: the card shows '—' with the note 'First-year cash flow ÷ $0.00 invested'.
findings.recommendation: When cashInvested is 0, use a note such as 'No cash invested, so cash-on-cash return is undefined'.

findings.evidence: The NOI formula 'NOI = rent × 12 × (1 − vacancy) − operating costs' and the assumption at line 100 ('percentages of rent actually collected') omit other monthly income, which the engine includes in GSI/EGI and in the percentage-cost base (src/calculators/rental-property.js:79-91). Vacancy also applies to other income.
findings.recommendation: Write '(rent + other income) × 12 × (1 − vacancy)' and 'percentages of income actually collected'.

findings.evidence: The branch range de965bd..HEAD also contains commit a47af1e (ZA-001 fix), which changes the shared monthlyPayment formula used by about 11 live calculators (mortgage, refinance, auto, personal, HELOC, home-equity, affordability, payoff, balance transfer, credit card payoff) and loosens the tolerance in tests/mortgage-payment.test.js:72,78 from 1e-8 to 1e-7. I checked the math: P·r/(−expm1(−n·log1p r)) equals the annuity formula; max |new − old| over P to $100M, rates 0.01–36%, terms 12–480 is $0.00006, and tiny rates now give finite P/n instead of Infinity. Behaviour change is benign and is a correctness improvement, but it is not part of the two drafts and touches live pages.
findings.recommendation: Keep it, but report it as its own change (ZA-001) separately from the draft calculators, and have the live calculators' browser/visual tests rerun before the next deploy.
